newsitem.title: USA: Sun Microsystems net surges on record sales.
newsitem.headline: Sun Microsystems net surges on record sales.

text.p: Computer maker Sun Microsystems Inc. said Thursday its net income nearly doubled in its fiscal fourth quarter, boosted by record-level sales as the company extends beyond its workstation franchise.

Profits climbed 94 percent to $237 million from $122 million in the year-ago period in the quarter ended June 30. Earnings per share surged to 61 cents vs. the year-ago figure of 31 cents, which included a one-time charge equal to 12 cents a share.
Revenues at the company, based in Mountain View, Calif., climbed 26 percent to $2.54 billion from $2.02 billion in the strong year-ago fourth quarter.
"Momentum is a wonderful thing," Chief Financial Officer Michael Lehman said in an upbeat conference call with analysts. "Our business model has never been stronger."
Sun's earnings, which were issued after the close of trading on Nasdaq, surpassed Wall Street's estimate of 59 cents a share, according to the First Call service.

After briefly dipping as low as $44.50 in the after-hours market, the stock rebounded, with one trade hitting as high as $47.5625 before settling in the $45.75-to-$46 range. Earlier Thursday, Sun Microsystems stock rose 56 cents a share to a new closing high of $45.56 on the Nasdaq market.
The stock had surged more than 22 percent since last Friday and has gained more than 75 percent since late April, as it set four consecutive record highs this week.

"We're excited about exiting the fiscal 1997 year at a $10 billion (revenue) run rate," said Sun Chairman Scott McNealy. "I've never seen more pure activity in our company than we're facing right now."

Like brands of soft drinks, he said Sun was asserting its position among the best-known names in computing, with a widening range of products like rivals Hewlett-Packard Co. and International Business Machines Corp..
Analysts said the enthusiasm of Sun's executives reflected a particularly strong business cycle, with new products due to come out across a broad spectrum in its new fiscal year.

"The list of new products, new directions, new opportunities is long at this point," said Goldman Sachs & Co. analyst Laura Conigliaro, commenting on the company's expansion into a more broad-based computer maker.
"It's not a product -- it's many products," she said.

Lehman said Sun had shipped a record number of systems in its fourth quarter. Ed Zander, president of Sun Microsystems Computer Co., said revenues from servers -- machines which tie networks of computers together -- had more than doubled year-over-year in the June quarter.
"They've got momentum," said J.P. Morgan analyst Daniel Kunstler. "They don't have competitiors in their space. ... They've got basically clear flying ahead of them. They've executed very well."

Lehman said the company expects to accelerate hiring early in the new fiscal year in areas that will boost revenue growth, while McNealy said the company will spend more than $1 billion on research and development in fiscal 1998.
"These guys are investing very very wisely. That's the story here," said Kunstler.
Before the earnings report, Sun said it had entered into a definitive agreement to acquire the assets of Encore Computer Corp.'s storage business at a purchase price of $185 million.
